title: Multiscale signed heartbeat asymmetry does not establish robust incremental age prediction across two public collections
abstract: Adding mean normalized cubic RR-increment asymmetry at lags 1, 2 and 4 to conventional HRV and low-order linear-dependence predictors reduced age-group transfer logloss by 0.021436 from Fantasia to NSR2 and 0.013373 in reverse. Source-and-target bootstrap 95% intervals were [-0.137972, 0.191465] and [-0.123578, 0.163397]. Sensitivity to recording duration, regularization and a single-lag asymmetry comparator prevents a robust incremental-biomarker claim. This is exploratory separate-collection transfer with historically reused data and unknown participant overlap.
